pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's C of E Nursery and Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
'Do unto others as you would have them do to you'. (Mt 7.12)
Welcome to St Matthew's Primary
Welcome to our website. I hope that it provides you with a picture of our school as an exciting, outward-looking school where academic attainment is very high and personal and moral development is carefully nurtured.
Within this Christian community, you will find children from different backgrounds, faiths and cultures working and playing harmoniously together.
Parent Tours
School tours take place on Tuesdays at 9:15am. To book a tour, please contact the school office on 02089477227 or office@st-matthews.merton.sch.uk
We look forward to welcoming you to St. Matthew's.
SIAMS Report

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's C of E Nursery and Primary School - School Values
pageCache.text:
'Do unto others as you would have them do to you'. (Mt 7.12)
School ValuesFriendship - Discovery -Prayer
Our school values are those of love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control . These are the Fruit of the Spirit from Galatians 5.22-23.
Each class has adopted their own Fruit of the Spirit and has used this as the basis for an artwork. Each half-term we focus on a particular Fruit of the Spirit, which informs our Collective Worship.
During the Spring term each class leads collective worship sharing their value with the rest of the school community.
SIAMS Report

'Do unto others as you would have them do to you'. (Mt 7.12)
Faith Champions
As Faith Champions we find ways to make our school live out the values. At the end of each half term we pick someone who has been showing the values and we award them a special certificate. When we have meetings we discuss competitions and ways which we can encourage faith in our school.
We lead assemblies where we learn about Jesus and his experiences. Picture News is something else we do where we vote about what we think about each question and it is really nice to learn about what others think. As Faith Champion I am in charge of the Picture News Poll.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's C of E Nursery and Primary School - Class Worship
pageCache.text:
'Do unto others as you would have them do to you'. (Mt 7.12)
Class Worship
Year 2
In year 2 class worship we read a creation story from the Bible and talked about how we were guardians of our world.
Year 3
Our class value is gentleness. We brought teddies and showed the school how to be gentle with them. We had a gentle word jar and every time someone was gentle, a pompom was put in the jar. In our drama show, Jesus was on the Mount of Olives showing gentleness towards Mary Magdalene. This was an example to show gentleness to all.
Year 4
In Year 4, our Class Worship subject was joy, which is our fruit of the spirit. We found out that there was a clothes shop named Joy (maybe because they liked selling stuff) but we were talking about the proper meaning. We sang an old Christian song which goes, ' Give me joy in my heart keep me praising, give me joy in my heart I pray, give me joy in my heart keep me praising, keep me praising till the break of day!'
We thought our topic was really important, because we should all express and feel joy as much as we can! We also looked at a quote from Mother Teresa, which helped us think about joy too.
Year 5
Our class value is patience. We did a class worship on patience. We acted out some scenes on how to be patient. One of them was not getting mad at yourself if you are struggling at something. Another one was being patient with others. We also performed a poem and thought about all the people in the bible who were patient, Job, Abraham and Sarah.
SIAMS Report

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's C of E Nursery and Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
'Do unto others as you would have them do to you'. (Mt 7.12)
Collective Worship
Every day all the children take part in an act of Collective Worship, where they have an opportunity to gather together, to reflect and to communicate with God. Sometimes the children will gather as a whole school, sometimes in Key Stages and sometimes in classes or House groups.
Our assemblies involve.....
Gathering
We gather together and greet each other. We all come to play a part in this community. We are preparing to meet with God.
Engaging
We engage with the big things and the little things in life. We encounter Jesus and the stories of the Bible. We are listening for God's message to us.
Responding
We respond to what we have heard and seen. We respond together and as individuals. We are given the opportunity to worship God.
Sending
We are sent out to love and serve one another and to make a difference in the world. We are all dismissed with God's blessing.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's C of E Nursery and Primary School - Our Church
pageCache.text:
'Do unto others as you would have them do to you'. (Mt 7.12)
Our Anglican Church
St Matthew’s is one of many Voluntary Aided Anglican schools within the Southwark Diocese and is one of five Anglican schools in the Local Authority. The school was established in the mid 1800s, when free state education was not available in England to the general public. The mission of the school was to provide a Christian education for local Anglican children and also to serve the local poor. The school continues to provide an education which is underpinned by the Fruits of the Spirit
Our Christian Values - Fruits of the Spirit
The school is very well supported by the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education, who give advice about the curriculum, staffing, admissions and premises. The grounds and the school building belong to the Church. As a Voluntary Aided school we have a certain amount of autonomy such as deciding on our Admissions Policy and our Religious Education curriculum. However the school community has a responsibility to maintain the fabric of the building, which is why parents are asked for a voluntary contribution each year.
All children, irrespective of faith position, are encouraged to view Southwark Cathedral as THEIR Cathedral. Our Year 6 children are made to feel very special at the Leavers’ Service which is held every July at Southwark Cathedral and which celebrates the children’s primary years and their transition to the next phase of their education.
Local Anglican Churches
The congregations of many of our local Anglican churches are represented in the school and there is a particularly strong link with St Matthew's Church.
The Vicar of St Matthew’s is a welcome presence in the school and a good friend to pupils and staff, providing support, guidance and more formal input in classroom work as well as assemblies. The children and staff attend the church for important celebrations such as Harvest Festival, the Carol Service, Easter Celebrations and the Leavers' Mass. We are especially proud that children of all faiths happily attend these services. Anglican children in Year Two and above are invited to participate in preparation for their First Communion .
The relationship between church and school is one of mutual support and learning which enriches both communities. Many members of the congregation volunteer at the school - hearing the children read and providing a perspective for the children on topics such as child evacuation in WW2. Members of the Wimbledon Team ministry, and especially St Matthew's Church make up a significant proportion of the School Governing Body.
SIAMS Report

pageCache.pageTitle: St Matthew's C of E Nursery and Primary School - Parents and Carers
pageCache.text:
'Do unto others as you would have them do to you'. (Mt 7.12)
Parents and Carers
Your Help is Invaluable
Parents are warmly invited to come in to school to support us, with everything from hearing readers or playing games with a small group of children to helping out with clubs or accompanying us on trips. If you think you might be able to help or you have a skill that might be useful to us, we would love to hear from you - your help really is invaluable.
Keeping You Informed
Our experience has demonstrated that children make the best progress when parents are fully engaged in their child’s learning. You will receive a Progress Report in the Autumn and Spring terms describing your child’s behaviour and attitudes and at the end of the year your child’s teacher will write a comprehensive report detailing your child’s attainment and effort in each area of the curriculum. We hold two parents’ evenings every year where you may discuss your child’s progress with their teacher.
Contact With Your Child's Class Teacher
We encourage frequent informal contact with your child’s class teacher ,who will always be willing to suggest ways in which you as a parent can support your child in their work. Teachers are always happy to see you at short notice to discuss any concerns you may have about your child’s education or welfare. We would much rather you came to us as soon as you are worried, rather than having sleepless nights. With your help we can in most cases resolve the problem quickly.
The Headteacher is always available to listen to parents - appointments can be made by contacting the office.
Workshops and Information Evenings
We hold occasional workshops on topical issues such as current techniques in maths teaching, home learning environments, reading and homework. Any suggestions for future evenings are welcomed - please contact the office.
